detail.title: Rational Criteria for Abandoning Research Agendas
detail.summary: This notebook explores rational abandonment criteria for research agendas, distinguishing between optimal stopping and cognitive biases like the sunk cost effect. It synthesizes findings from human decision-making literature and computational planning models to propose that rational abandonment requires explicitly separating the expected future epistemic utility from the resources already invested.
detail.reason: The project p-question-abandonment-001 is synthesis-ready, and this notebook formalizes the rational criteria based on retrieved sources.

detail.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment
detail.summary: This revised notebook synthesizes findings on sunk cost bias and adaptive planning to propose criteria for the rational abandonment of research agendas, emphasizing the need to decouple previous investments from future strategic utility.
detail.reason: Incorporating new evidence on policy frameworks to expand the scope of abandonment criteria beyond psychological bias.
